transcript: The voice is the first thing viewers judge in a narrated video. Here's how to choose a narrator voice and speed that let your content do the talking.
Don't judge a voice on its sample sentence. Paste in a real paragraph with the hard bits: names, numbers, acronyms. Compare two or three, then pick the easiest to follow.
Speed matters as much as the voice. Too slow feels patronising, too fast loses people. If captions flick past, slow down; if you want to skip, speed up.
A synthetic narrator reads exactly what you write. So 'Q3 rev. up 8%' becomes 'Revenue in the third quarter rose eight per cent.'
Each slide stays up as long as its narration lasts. For quiet slides or silent loops, set a minimum time per slide so nothing flashes past.
On Pro, a.i. directs the video, timing each animated scene to your narration. Try Basic first, then hear your deck at powerpoint2vid.com.
